{{Short description|none}} [[File:Congressional Districts of Cavite.svg|275px|thumb|{{center|Map of Cavite's congressional districts since 2018}}]] {{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of Cavite''' are the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Cavite]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national and local legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. At present, the province is represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] by its '''eight congressional districts''', with the districts' representatives being elected every three years. The congressional districts are coextensive with the provincial board districts, where each district is allotted two seats in the [[Cavite Provincial Board]], creating a total of sixteen elective seats in the legislature. == History == Cavite initially comprised a single district in 1898, when it elected four representatives to the [[Malolos Congress]] that lasted until 1899. The district was recreated in 1907 for the [[Philippine Assembly]],{{cite PH act|chamber=Act|number=1582|date=January 9, 1907|url=https://lawyerly.ph/laws/view/l5054|title=An Act to Provide for the Holding of Elections in the Philippine Islands, for the Organization of the Philippine Assembly, and for Other Purposes|accessdate=September 4, 2022}} this time electing one representative at-large. When seats for the [[Senate of the Philippines|upper house]] of the [[Philippine Legislature]] were elected from territory-based districts between 1916 and 1935, the province formed part of the [[Senatorial districts of the Philippines#Fifth District|fifth senatorial district]] which elected two out of the 24-member senate. In the disruption caused by the [[Second World War]], [[#1943–1944|two delegates]] represented the province in the [[National Assembly of the Second Philippine Republic|National Assembly]] of the Japanese-sponsored [[Second Philippine Republic]]: one was the provincial governor (an [[ex officio member|''ex officio'' member]]), while the other was elected through a provincial assembly of [[KALIBAPI]] members during the [[Japanese occupation of the Philippines]]. [[Cavite City]], being a chartered city, was [[Legislative district of Cavite City|represented separately]] in this short-lived legislative body. [[Tagaytay]], the province's other chartered city, was placed under provincial jurisdiction during the war and was not represented separately. Upon the restoration of the [[Philippine Commonwealth]] in 1945, the province and its two cities reverted to the pre-war lone district representation. The province was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region IV-A]] from 1978 to 1984, and returned [[#1984–1986|three representatives, elected at large]], to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]]. Cavite was reapportioned into three [[House of Representatives of the Philippines#District representation|congressional districts]] under the new Constitution{{cite web|author=1986 Constitutional Commission|title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance|url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|date=February 2, 1987|access-date=June 13, 2016}} which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987, and elected members to the restored House of Representatives starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]]. The passage of Republic Act No. 9727{{cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=9727|title=An Act Reapportioning The Province Of Cavite Into Seven (7) Legislative Districts|date=October 22, 2009|access-date=June 13, 2016|author=Congress of the Philippines|url=http://www.senate.gov.ph/republic_acts/ra%209727.pdf |url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120221232525/http://www.senate.gov.ph/republic_acts/ra%209727.pdf|archive-date=February 21, 2012}} on October 22, 2009, increased the number of the province's representatives from three to seven, starting in the [[2010 Philippine general election|2010 elections]]. However, the conversion of [[Dasmariñas]] into a city has resulted in an additional legal name for the [[#4th District|fourth district]], which became the [[Legislative district of Dasmariñas|Lone District of Dasmariñas]] after the ratification of Republic Act No. 9723{{cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=9723|title=An Act Converting the Municipality of Dasmariñas in the Province Of Cavite into a Component City to be Known as the City of Dasmariñas|date=October 15, 2009|access-date=June 13, 2016|url=http://www.senate.gov.ph/republic_acts/ra%209723.pdf |url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110611235719/http://www.senate.gov.ph/republic_acts/ra%209723.pdf|archive-date=June 11, 2011}} on November 25, 2009. Meanwhile, despite the conversion of [[Bacoor]] and [[Imus]] into cities in 2012, their charters explicitly indicate the retention of their numerical designations as the [[#2nd District|second]]{{cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=10160|url=http://www.lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2012/ra_10160_2012.html|title=An Act converting the municipality of Bacoor in the province of Cavite into a component city to be known as the City of Bacoor|date=April 10, 2012|access-date=June 13, 2016|author=Congress of the Philippines}} and [[#3rd District|third districts]]{{cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=10161|url=http://www.lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2012/ra_10161_2012.html|title=An Act converting the municipality of Imus in the province of Cavite into a component city to be known as the City of Imus|date=April 10, 2012|access-date=June 13, 2016|author=Congress of the Philippines}} of the province. Republic Act No. 11069, signed into law on September 17, 2018, reapportioned Cavite into eight legislative districts — the most for any province — by creating a separate legislative district for the newly converted city of [[General Trias]].{{cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=11069|url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/2018/09/14/republic-act-no-11069/ |title=An Act Amending Section 1 of Republic Act No. 9727, Reapportioning the Province of Cavite into Eight (8) Legislative Districts|date=August 23, 2018|access-date=July 22, 2019|author=Congress of the Philippines}} This effectively supersedes RA No. 9723 and confirms the sole legal designation of the congressional district of [[Dasmariñas]] as the [[#4th District|fourth district]] of Cavite. == Current congressional districts == The province's current congressional delegation composes of five members of the [[National Unity Party (Philippines)|National Unity Party]], one member of [[Lakas–CMD]] and one member of the [[Nationalist People's Coalition]]. {| class="wikitable sortable" style="margin: 1em auto; font-size:100%; line-height:20px; text-align:center" |+Legislative districts and representatives of [[Cavite]] ! rowspan="2" |District ! colspan="4" |Current Representative ! rowspan="2" |Constituent [[Local government in the Philippines|LGUs]] ! rowspan="2" |Population (2024){{cite web|url=https://psa.gov.ph/sites/default/files/attachments/ird/specialrelease/2_Table%201%20Population%20of%20Legislative%20Districts%20by%20Province%20and%20Selected%20HUC_Component%20City%20Web%20Final-signed.pdf |title=TABLE 1.
